headline: Coordinating Visits to Historic Monuments and Museums
reservation: Entry to the Legacy Museum and the National Memorial for Peace and Justice involves timed tickets which are highly recommended for weekend visits. While many government buildings allow public walk-ins, checking the current security protocol for the State Capitol is advised. Hotel availability is stable, but downtown rooms may spike during major civil rights anniversaries.

days.title: Civil Rights and State History

stops.name: Alabama State Capitol
stops.detail: Visit the site where the 1965 Selma-to-Montgomery march concluded and tour the historic chambers.

stops.name: Dexter Avenue King Memorial Baptist Church
stops.detail: See the pulpit where Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. preached and guided the Montgomery Bus Boycott.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes for city transit; these sites are within walking distance on Dexter Avenue.
days.note: Church tours are often led by guides and may have limited hours on weekdays.

days.title: Reflective Monuments and The Arts

stops.name: National Memorial for Peace and Justice
stops.detail: Walk through the outdoor memorial dedicated to the victims of lynching, designed as a space for reflection.

stops.name: Montgomery Museum of Fine Arts
stops.detail: Located in Blount Cultural Park, this museum features significant collections of American art and studio glass.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes for travel; the museum is a short drive from the downtown memorial sites.
days.note: The memorial is an outdoor space; prepare for varying humidity and heat during the summer.

days.title: Literary Icons and River Views
days.start: Suggested: 10:00 AM from Old Alabama Town

stops.name: F. Scott and Zelda Fitzgerald Museum
stops.detail: Explore the only museum in the world dedicated to the lives of the Fitzgeralds in their former home.

stops.name: Riverfront Park
stops.detail: Enjoy the views of the Alabama River and visit the Harriott II Riverboat docked near the historic amphitheater.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for transit; traffic is generally light outside of standard commuting hours.
days.note: Riverboat cruises operate on a specific seasonal schedule; verify departure days online.

intel.title: Government District
intel.text: Public parking lots are available near the EJI sites. Street parking is often free on weekends but check local signage carefully.

intel.title: Downtown Coverage
intel.text: Strong 5G signal is available throughout the downtown corridor. Dead zones are rare within the city limits.

intel.title: I-65 Access
intel.text: Fuel stations are concentrated at the interchanges of I-65 and I-85. Prices are consistent with regional Alabama averages.

intel.title: Museum Last Entry
intel.text: The Legacy Museum has a strict last-entry time that is usually an hour before closing. Plan your afternoon to arrive well before the cutoff.

intel.title: Walkability
intel.text: The 'Civil Rights Trail' through downtown is well-marked but involves some moderate inclines. Wear comfortable shoes for the Dexter Avenue walk.

plan.arrival: Arrive at MGM and take the 20-minute drive to downtown. Most major hotels and supply shops are located near the I-85 corridor.
plan.vehicle: A standard car is sufficient for all Montgomery sights. The city layout is grid-based and easy to navigate for non-local drivers.
plan.goldenHour: The Alabama Riverfront at sunset; light on the water is best viewed from the upper deck of the Riverfront Park amphitheater.

sources.label: Alabama Department of Archives and History
